map.在 4–24 的网格上手工点击上色绘制像素画，颜色从固定 6 色（红、橙、绿、蓝: Paint pixel art by hand on a 4-24 grid using one of six fixed colors (red, orange, green, blue, purple, black), then export character art as .txt or CSS box-shadow pixel blocks. It does not import images or pixelate automatically.

Grid size ranges from 4 to 24 and out-of-range values report an error; 8x8 loads a preset smiley with 48 filled cells, while other sizes start blank. The result area shows both the clickable canvas and a character-art preview: filled cells are ■ and empty ones ·, with each row holding as many symbols as the grid side. map.改变网格尺寸会按新尺寸重建画布并清空已绘内容（8×8 例外，载入预置笑脸）；本页: Changing the grid size rebuilds the canvas at the new size and clears existing artwork (8x8 is the exception and loads the preset smiley). This page does not rescale or resample, so export first if you want to keep the drawing. The drawing lives only in page memory and resets on refresh. The tool runs entirely in the front end: drawing and exports happen locally, and artwork is neither saved nor uploaded.
map.导出的字符画能直接贴进 README 吗？: Can the exported character art go straight into a README?
map.可以。字符画以 ■ 表示有色格、· 表示空白，每行符号数等于网格边长；贴进代码块: Yes. Character art uses ■ for filled cells and · for empty ones, with each row holding as many symbols as the grid side. It stays aligned inside a code block with a monospace font; a proportional font can make symbol widths uneven and cause misalignment.
